name: Amiodarone
executiveSummary: Class III antiarrhythmic (mixed effects). Arrest/VT: **300 mg IV** bolus → **150 mg**. Stable VT: **150 mg over 10 min** then **1 mg/min × 6 h** → **0.5 mg/min**. Chronic PO: load **400–800 mg/day** for weeks → maintenance **100–200 mg/day**. Thyroid/lung/liver toxicity.
indications:
## Indications

- Life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias; AF (rhythm control) when other options fail.
- Cardiac arrest (refractory VT/VF) per ACLS.

## Precautions

- Very long half-life; interactions (warfarin, digoxin, simvastatin — reduce doses).
- Monitor TSH, LFTs, chest X-ray, eyes in chronic use.
- Bradycardia, QT, IV hypotension.

> IV: preferably dilute in D5W; pump concentrations per protocol.

adulto.dose: Arrest: **300 mg IV** (diluted) → **150 mg** if persists. Pulse VT: **150 mg IV over 10 min**; infusion **1 mg/min × 6 h** then **0.5 mg/min**. PO: load **400–800 mg/day** (up to 1.2 g) × 1–3 weeks → **100–200 mg/day**.
adulto.administration: IV in D5W; PO with food if intolerant. Central line preferred at high concentrations.

pediatrico.dose: Arrest: **5 mg/kg IV** (max 300) → repeat **5 mg/kg**. Infusion: **5–15 µg/kg/min**. PO: load/maintenance by cardiology (~**5–10 mg/kg/day** load).

stability:
## Stability

- Infusion: protect from light; limited PVC stability — preferred sets.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

IV hypotension, bradycardia; chronic: hypo/hyperthyroidism, pulmonary fibrosis, ↑ enzymes, corneal deposits, photosensitivity, blue-gray skin.

ESC. Ventricular arrhythmias / AF rhythm control.
